newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Nearly 750 fishing crew missing in Bangladesh storm.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 750 fishing crew missing in Bangladesh storm.

text.p: Nearly 750 fishermen were reported missing on Thursday in the Bay of Bengal, three days after a cyclone battered the Bangladesh coast killing around 100 people.
In storm-battered coastal areas, people returned home from cyclone shelters and officials said all measures had been taken to prevent any outbreak of disease or hunger.
"About 750 of our men are still missing," said Kabir Ahmed, leader of the Mechanised Fishing Boats Association in Cox's Bazar.
"They went to sea before the cyclone struck on Monday but did not return.
"We only hope they would come back alive," he told Reuters. "But no official search has been launched to find the missing fishermen."
Some 1,500 fishermen were reported missing on Tuesday, but Ahmed and other association leaders said half of them had returned by Wednesday evening.
"In the event of every storm, scores of fishing crew drown in the Bay of Bengal because they cannot get to shore in time despite hearing storm warnings over the radio," Ahmed said.
Officials in Cox's Bazar said the fishermen often ignore warnings for the lure of a big catch.
"Some boats don't have radio or their engines are not strong enough to combat high waves," one official said.
"There has been no information yet of outbreak of disease or people facing starvation from anywhere in the affected areas," Chittagong district administrator K.M.M. Habibullah said.
"We are keeping a constant vigil and speeding up reflief supplies," he said.
"As of now there is no shortage of drinking water or medical assistance for the cyclone survivors. Hundreds of medical teams are working."

Jawadul Karim, press secretary to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, told reporters on Wednesday that nearly 2.5 million peopl were affected by the cyclone that roared in from the Bay of Bengal, packing winds up to 200 kph (125 mph).

The official BSS news agency, quoting figures available from the disaster control room at Hasina's office, on Thursday put the confirmed death toll by Thursday at 105 -- still down from the 121 earlier reported by police and officials.
BSS said at least 9,663 people were injured and 612,000 houses damaged.
The U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs in Geneva said on Wednesday that the cyclone had killed at least 200 people.
Low-lying Bangladesh is prone to devastation from cyclones. The country's worst storm in 1991 killed at least 138,000 people and left millions homeless.
Officials in the port city of Chittagong, which also suffered badly in Monday's cyclone, said on Tuesday nearly 1.5 million people were made homeless. They said thousands of cattle were killed.
Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad on Thursday briefed foreign diplomats in Dhaka on Thursday about the devastation wrought by the cyclone, officials said. But they declined to give details.
Cox's Bazar officials said some fishermen had started going back to sea from storm-battered islands on Thursday, while the fate of others remained unknown.
"Fishing is their only living, they just can't sit idle," one official said. "Besides, they are used to the situation."
Navy vessels helping in relief operation among off-shore islands had received no orders to search for the missing fishermen, navy sources in Chittagong said on Thursday.

Prime Minister Hasina has visited most of the affected areas over the past two days to supervise relief and rescue efforts. Survivors told her they needed help to rebuild their homes first, officials said.
